title: Arbitrary base change for smooth ambient duality
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $N\geq1$ satisfy $NA=0$, with $N$ invertible on the schemes in question, as in [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. All categories are the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], not completed or constructible categories. For a morphism $v$, write $v^*$ for exact etale inverse image on constant-coefficient module sheaves, extended degreewise to complexes. Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth, separated, compactifiable and of pure relative dimension $d$, between Noetherian schemes, as in [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. Let $g:S'\to S$ be any morphism of Noetherian schemes, and put $X'=X\times_S S'$, with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$. Use $Rf_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and its right adjoint $f^\times$ of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and similarly for $f'$. The canonical morphism $\beta_{f,g,K}:g'^*f^\times K\to f'^\times g^*K$, obtained by transposing the pullback of the counit through compact-support base change, is an isomorphism for every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. At $K=A_S$ it gives $b:g'^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f'}$, where $\omega_f=f^\times A_S$. If $\phi_{f,K}:f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\to f^\times K$ denotes the canonical tensor map of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], then
$$\beta_{f,g,K}\circ g'^*\phi_{f,K}=\phi_{f',g^*K}\circ(1\otimes b)$$
after identifying $g'^*(f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)$ with $f'^*g^*K\otimes_A^Lg'^*\omega_f$. The derived tensor is the ringed-site tensor construction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to the constant ring on the etale site.

proof.text: Use [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] for the given finite ring $A$. It supplies compactification-independent $Rf_!$, associative composition, and the canonical exchange $C_{f,g}:g^*Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!g'^*$ on the entire ordinary small-etale derived categories. Its normalization on a chosen compactification $f=rj$ is proper exchange for $r$ followed by the inverse open-extension comparison for $j$. This is precisely the comparison used in the blueprint's first paragraph, now on arbitrary unbounded inputs. All compactification schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since the proper factor is finite type over its Noetherian base. The lemma also gives equality of the comparisons under refinement, composition of morphisms and successive changes of base. Thus no bounded-below truncation argument is needed.

source.place: Paragraph 1 and coherence (i); Stacks 0F7H, 0F7I, 0F7J, 0F7K, 0F7L (more-etale.tex, section-derived-lower-shriek-compactification and its lemmas)

proof.text:
By [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], define $\beta_{f,g,K}$ as the adjunct under $Rf'_!\dashv f'^\times$ of $g^*\epsilon_{f,K}\circ C_{f,g,f^\times K}^{-1}$. Its defining equation is
$$\epsilon_{f',g^*K}\circ Rf'_!(\beta_{f,g,K})=g^*\epsilon_{f,K}\circ C_{f,g,f^\times K}^{-1}.$$
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the inverse exchanges of Step 1. Clause (2) says that the mate for a composite of morphisms is the composite of their mates, using the composite adjunction; clause (1) gives the analogous equality for successive changes of base. Clause (3) transports these equations through the counit-preserving comparisons between chosen right adjoints. These are equations of the specified maps and will identify the model and chart maps below.

source.place: Paragraph 1: transposition of the counit; coherences (i)–(iii)

proof.text:
For a fixed compactification $f=rj$ and arbitrary $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $Q\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] gives the ordered isomorphism
$$Q\otimes^LRr_*j_!M\longrightarrow Rr_*(r^*Q\otimes^Lj_!M).$$
Here $r$ is proper of finite type between Noetherian schemes and $A$ is finite; that lemma requires neither boundedness nor Tor amplitude. Apply [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] to $j$, $M$ and $r^*Q$, and conjugate by tensor symmetry, to identify its target with $Rf_!(f^*Q\otimes^LM)$. Denote the resulting compact-support projection isomorphism by $P_{f,Q,M}$. It has the order $Q\otimes^LRf_!M\to Rf_!(f^*Q\otimes^LM)$ required by the canonical tensor morphism in [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. The same construction applies to the pulled-back compactification.

source.place: Final paragraph: the compact-support projection map; Stacks 0GL1 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor)

proof.text: The open tensor comparison in Step 3 commutes with arbitrary base change. Indeed identify $g_{\overline X}^*j_!$ with $j'_!g'^*$ using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules]. Transpose the two maps in the proposed square under $j'_!\dashv j'^*$ of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. The open tensor map is induced by the sheaf tensor identity on restriction [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]; the extension comparison is the adjoint comparison of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. After restriction both transposes are the identity on $g'^*M\otimes^Lf'^*g^*Q$, with the pullback/tensor identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Hence the adjunction bijection makes the maps equal. This uses equality after an adjunction bijection, not faithfulness of geometric stalks on derived morphisms.

source.place: Final paragraph: open part of the projection/exchange square; Stacks 03S6, 0GL1, 07A4

proof.text:
For the proper factor $r$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] gives the commuting square between its counit-defined projection map and proper exchange on arbitrary unbounded complexes. Its tensor order is $(j_!M,Q)$; conjugate the square by the two tensor symmetries to obtain the order in [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. This conjugation respects pullback: on total tensor complexes the swap in bidegree $(a,b)$ multiplies by $(-1)^{ab}$, and inverse image preserves degrees and this scalar. Naturality of symmetry gives the corresponding equality at the direct-image end. Pasting with the open square of Step 4 gives the equality
$$C_{f,g,f^*Q\otimes^LM}\,g^*P_{f,Q,M}=P_{f',g^*Q,g'^*M}\,(1\otimes C_{f,g,M}),$$
with canonical pullback/tensor identifications inserted. Inverting the projection maps gives the corresponding equation for $P^{-1}$; no boundedness restriction occurs.

source.place: Final paragraph: proper part and pasting of the projection/exchange square; Stacks 0E48 (sites-cohomology.tex, remark-compatible-with-diagram), 07A4

proof.text:
For $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, use [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] with the given $A,N$. Its ordinary finite-etale twist is $L_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$, its right adjoint is $G_qK=q^*K\otimes^LL_P(1)[2]$, and its counit is $(1\otimes t_q)P_q^{-1}$, where $t_q=\operatorname{pr}_2b_q^{-1}$. Its decomposition and trace commute with canonical proper exchange. Explicitly, with $\rho:g_P^*L_P(1)\cong L_{P'}(1)$ from [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and $B=Rq'_*(\rho[2])\operatorname{Ex}_{q,L_P(1)[2]}$, this says $B\,g^*b_q=b_{q'}(\rho_S[2]\oplus1)$. Consequently $t_{q'}B=g^*t_q$, by multiplying by the inverse decomposition and projecting to the second summand. Let $a:g_P^*G_qK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{q'}g^*K$ be pullback/tensor/twist comparison. Step 5 and this trace equation give
$$\epsilon_{q',g^*K}Rq'_!(a)=g^*\epsilon_{q,K}C_{q,g,G_qK}^{-1}.$$
Under the counit-preserving identification of $G_q$ with $q^\times$ (and the primed identification), this is exactly Step 2's defining equation. The adjunction bijection gives $a=\beta_{q,g,K}$; hence the canonical mate is invertible.

source.place: Paragraph 2 and coherence (ii): ordinary finite-coefficient projective-line model and specified trace/counit

proof.text: Use the exact etale compact-support and exchange normalization of [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]. Let $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$. Compose $j_!\dashv j^*$ with the projective-line adjunction. The open comparison is the comparison of left adjoints specified in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]; its mate is ordinary restriction comparison. Thus its counit commutes with the pullback square. The pasting identity along adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the mate for $p_1=qj$ with the composite of this restriction comparison and the isomorphism in Step 6. The resulting right adjoint is $p_1^*(1)[2]$. For $d=0$ use the identity adjunction. For $d+1$ factor $p_{d+1}$ as an affine-line projection followed by $p_d$; Step 1 identifies the composite left adjoint, and the same mate-pasting identity identifies its exchange with the composite of the already invertible exchanges. The twist/pullback and tensor identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] give $p_{d+1}^*(d+1)[2d+2]$. This induction uses the explicit composite adjunction, and compares its right adjoint directly with the ambient right adjoint of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] by the unique counit-preserving comparison. The imported affine-space adjunction with its pro-etale twist dependency is not used.

source.place: Paragraph 2: open restriction from the projective line, then induction on affine-space dimension

proof.text: For every separated finite-type etale $u:U\to X$, [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] identifies compactification-defined $Ru_!$ with the exact sum-extension functor, preserving its evaluation counit. It also states the exchange equation $(c_{u'}h^*)C_{u,g}=C^\Sigma_{u,g}(g^*c_u)$, with the same proper/open normalization as Step 1. The sum-extension comparison of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules] has as mate the inverse-image composition isomorphism: substitute its defining adjoint comparison into the counit equation of Step 2; the two triangles cancel the unit and counit. Thus its mate is invertible. Use [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] and clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] for $fu$. Under $u^*f^\times\cong(fu)^\times$ and the primed comparison, $\beta_{fu,g,K}$ is the composite of $u'^*\beta_{f,g,K}$ with this invertible etale mate. In particular either of these two maps is invertible exactly when the other is. This identifies the actual canonical maps on source charts.

source.place: Coherence (iii): counit-preserving etale normalization and source-chart locality; Stacks 03S6 and 0GL9

proof.text: For base restriction write $a:S_0\hookrightarrow S$, $a_X:X_0\hookrightarrow X$, and $f_0:X_0\to S_0$, so $fa_X=af_0$. Compact-support composition from [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identifies $Rf_!a_{X!}$ with $a_!Rf_{0!}$. Taking their right adjoints using [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] identifies $a_X^*f^\times$ with $f_0^\times a^*$, preserving the composite counits. The same holds for $a':S'_0\hookrightarrow S'$. These comparisons are the mates of the open base-restriction exchanges: the left-adjoint comparison is the proper/open exchange of Step 1 and the exact open comparison normalized in [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]. If $g_0:S'_0\to S_0$ is induced by $g$, then $ga'=ag_0$. The two pasting equations for $C$ give the same exchange for this common composite. Take their mates using clauses (1) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. One is the primed restriction comparison composed with $a'_X{}^*\beta_{f,g,K}$; the other is $\beta_{f_0,g_0,a^*K}$ composed with the unprimed restriction comparison. Their equality identifies the restricted canonical map with the base-chart map.

source.place: Coherences (i) and (iii): compatibility of the canonical mate with an open restriction in the base

proof.text: Apply [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] at each point of $X$. After an affine open restriction in the base, choose an affine open $U\subseteq X$ and an etale $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_{S_0}$ with $fu=p_de$. The relative dimension is $d$, since the etale factor has relative dimension zero and $f$ has pure relative dimension $d$. The chart inclusion $u$ is separated and of finite type: it is an open immersion, and it is quasi-compact because $X$ is Noetherian. The map $e$ is separated since $U$ and $\mathbf A^d_{S_0}$ are affine: on rings its diagonal is given by the surjection $B\otimes_R B\to B$, $b\otimes b'\mapsto bb'$. It is locally of finite presentation since it is etale, and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since $U$ is affine and $\mathbf A^d_{S_0}$ is quasi-separated. Hence $e$ is of finite type. They are compactifiable, as are their composites, by [thm-nagata-compactification]. The charts, their affine-space targets, and their base changes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. After arbitrary base change the corresponding open charts still cover $X'$. Steps 7–9 identify the restriction of $\beta_{f,g,K}$ on each chart with etale inverse image of the affine-space isomorphism. Thus it is an isomorphism on every chart. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] commutes with cohomology; the kernel and cokernel of each cohomology map vanish on that etale covering, so their sections vanish by the sheaf axiom. Equivalently this is [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-detects-iso] applied to the underlying abelian cohomology sheaves. Hence every cohomology map is invertible globally, and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] proves that $\beta_{f,g,K}$ is invertible in the unbounded derived category.

source.place: Coherence (iii): etale normal forms and descent on cohomology; Stacks 054L

proof.text: At $K=A_S$, exact inverse image preserves the constant coefficient unit, so Step 10 gives $b:g'^*\omega_f\cong\omega_{f'}$. To check the tensor square, recall the meaning of the canonical tensor morphism: it is the transpose of $Rf_!(f^*K\otimes^L\omega_f)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}K\otimes^LRf_!\omega_f\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{f,A}}K$. Transpose both proposed paths under $Rf'_!\dashv f'^\times$. The transpose of the upper path is the pullback of this displayed composite preceded by $C^{-1}$. The transpose of the lower path is the primed projection inverse followed by $1\otimes Rf'_!b$ and $1\otimes\epsilon_{f',A}$. Step 5 identifies their projection-formula factors; the defining equation of $b$ from Step 2 identifies their final factors, since $\epsilon_{f',A}Rf'_!b=g^*\epsilon_{f,A}C^{-1}$. Naturality of $C$ and tensor lets these substitutions be made in the composite. The transposes are equal, so the adjunction bijection proves the displayed tensor compatibility. [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] ensures these canonical tensor maps are the claimed isomorphisms.

source.place: Final paragraph: the two transposes of the tensor-compatibility rectangle

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be as in
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor], and let $g:S'\to S$
be any morphism of Noetherian schemes. Denote its base
change by $f':X'\to S'$, with $g':X'\to X$.
The canonical morphism

$$
g'^*f^\times K\longrightarrow f'^\times g^*K
$$

is an isomorphism for every complex $K$. At $K=A$
it identifies $g'^*\omega_f$ with $\omega_{f'}$,
and it respects the tensor isomorphism of
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor].

proof.text:
Proper base change on a compactification, followed by the
stalkwise base-change identity for extension by zero, gives
$Rf'_!g'^*\cong g^*Rf_!$, for bounded-below complexes by the
finite-amplitude argument in
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. Define the
displayed map by the adjunction of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], transposing

$$
Rf'_!g'^*f^\times K\cong g^*Rf_!f^\times K
\longrightarrow g^*K.
$$

For a projective-line projection its unit and counit are
those explicitly constructed in
[thm-amb-p1-adjunction]. Both commute with base change:
the supported diagonal class does so by
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], and the trace does so
by [thm-amb-p1-decomposition]. Hence the displayed
map in that case is the ordinary inverse-image and twist
base-change isomorphism. The same holds for an affine-line
projection by restricting its projective compactification,
and for affine space by composing those adjunctions.

It remains to verify the three coherences on which the identification
rests; each is a statement about the canonical maps, not merely about
their sources and targets.
*(i) The underlying base-change map in the model case.*
For the affine-space projection $\mathbf A^d_{S_0}\to S_0$
over a Zariski open $S_0\subseteq S$, the identification
$Rf'_!g'^*\cong g^*Rf_!$ of the first paragraph is the composite of
proper base change for the compactification
$\mathbf A^d\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^d$ with the stalkwise identity
$g^*j_!=j'_!g'^*$ for the extension by zero; both are comparisons of
the two diagrams obtained by base changing one diagram along $g$,
so the composite restricts to the chart $S'_0=S'\times_SS_0$.
*(ii) Unit and counit on the chart.* There the adjunction of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] is the affine-space adjunction
[cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], whose unit and counit are built
from the trace and the supported diagonal class; these commute with
base change by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] and
[thm-amb-p1-decomposition]. The displayed map is the transpose of
the counit composite, so the base-change isomorphism of (i) carries it
to the corresponding transpose over $S'_0$, which is the map defined
by the same recipe there.
*(iii) Descent to $X'$.* On the etale chart of $f$ used in
the proof of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor],
[lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] identifies the map under
consideration with the base-change isomorphism of (ii) preceded by
etale inverse image, the sum over the finite fibre commuting with base
change; it is therefore an isomorphism on an etale cover of $X'$,
hence everywhere. Finally the tensor maps of
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor] were transposed from the projection
formula and the counit, and applying the same transposition to the
commuting base-change diagram of those two maps gives their base-change
compatibility. This proves all the claimed identifications.
